g.text: A flat-plate boundary layer grows downstream and can transition from laminar to turbulent flow

text.style: font-size: 9px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #59636c

g.text: Flat plate with nominal zero pressure gradient. Laminar and turbulent thickness trends are blended across an assigned0.6–0.9 m transition region for
illustration, not a solved transitional boundary layer. Surface roughness, disturbances, pressure gradient, and free-stream turbulence affect transition.
Boundary-layer edge is a conventional thickness, not a sharp physical interface.
